queries.query: A software company agrees to build a bespoke AI recruitment platform for £180,000, promising delivery by 1 June. The contract states that “time is of the essence” and limits the supplier’s liability to £25,000. The platform is delivered on 20 June. Several important functions do not work, and the customer claims that the delay caused it to lose a commercial contract worth £300,000. The supplier argues that the customer would probably have lost the contract anyway and that the exclusion clause limits any recovery. Advise the customer on breach, classification of contractual terms, termination, causation, remoteness, mitigation, damages and the enforceability of the limitation clause.
queries.subject: contract

queries.query: Maya buys a £4,500 laptop from TechHub Ltd after a salesperson tells her that it is “specifically designed for professional 8K video editing” and will remain suitable for at least five years. Within four months, the laptop repeatedly overheats when Maya edits 8K footage. TechHub relies on written terms stating that sales staff cannot make binding representations and that the customer’s only remedy is repair. The manufacturer offers to replace an internal component but refuses a refund. Advise Maya on satisfactory quality, fitness for purpose, description, pre-contract statements, statutory remedies, repair, replacement, rejection, misrepresentation and attempts to restrict consumer rights.
queries.subject: consumer

queries.query: “The modern law governing duties of care is not based on one coherent legal test, but on a collection of policy-driven exceptions.” Critically assess this statement. Your answer should consider incremental development, assumption of responsibility, omissions, public-authority liability, pure economic loss and the role of foreseeability, proximity, fairness and precedent.
queries.subject: tort

queries.query: During a protest, Aaron deliberately pushes a security officer in order to move him away from a doorway. The officer falls, strikes his head and suffers a serious injury. Because of an undiagnosed medical condition, the injury becomes fatal. Later that night, Ben believes that the officer is still alive and strikes him with a metal bar, intending to kill him. Medical evidence shows that the officer had probably died shortly before Ben struck him, although the time of death cannot be established conclusively. Advise Aaron and Ben on homicide, unlawful act manslaughter, causation, mens rea, attempts and any relevant defences.
queries.subject: criminal

queries.query: A solicitor uses an AI limitation-calculation tool when advising a client about a negligence claim. The tool produces the wrong date, and the solicitor fails to verify it manually. Proceedings are commenced after the applicable limitation period has expired. The solicitor argues that the client failed to provide complete medical records and that the underlying negligence claim had only a 40% chance of success. Advise the client on duty, breach, scope of duty, causation, loss of a chance, contributory negligence, recoverable loss and the relevance of the solicitor’s reliance on AI.
queries.subject: professional negligence

queries.query: “The English courts’ power to exclude improperly obtained evidence gives defendants weaker protection than a strict exclusionary rule would provide.” Critically assess this statement. Consider confessions, oppression, unreliability, improperly obtained evidence, fairness, identification evidence, hearsay and judicial discretion. Address the competing objectives of reliable fact-finding, protection of defendants and public confidence in criminal justice.
queries.subject: criminal evidence

queries.query: A technology company introduces an AI system that scores employees for promotion and redundancy. The system gives lower scores to older workers; women returning from maternity leave; disabled employees with periods of sickness absence; and employees who previously complained about discrimination. Several employees are dismissed after managers rely on the scores without conducting independent assessments. The employer argues that the system was designed by an external supplier and was intended to improve efficiency. Advise the affected employees and the employer on unfair dismissal, redundancy, direct and indirect discrimination, discrimination arising from disability, reasonable adjustments, victimisation, justification, evidential burdens and remedies.
queries.subject: employment and equality

queries.query: A owns registered freehold land. A orally promises B that B may live in the property for life if B pays for major renovations. B spends £120,000 improving the property and moves into it. A subsequently grants C a seven-year lease, but the lease is not registered. A then sells the property to D. D knows that B occupies the property but makes no detailed enquiries. D argues that neither B nor C has a registered interest. Advise B, C and D on proprietary estoppel, constructive trusts where relevant, leases, overriding interests, actual occupation, priorities and registration.
queries.subject: land

queries.query: “Judicial review has developed from a mechanism for controlling the legal limits of government power into a constitutional system for protecting substantive rights.” Critically evaluate this proposition. Your answer should consider illegality, procedural fairness, legitimate expectation, irrationality, proportionality, justiciability, ouster clauses and the constitutional relationship between Parliament, the executive and the courts.
queries.subject: public and constitutional

queries.query: The directors of Alpha Ltd learn that a major customer wishes to award Alpha a valuable supply contract. One director secretly forms a separate company and causes the customer to award the contract to that company instead. The same director also receives an undisclosed payment from a supplier. After discovering the conduct, the controlling shareholders pass a resolution purporting to approve everything the director has done. A minority shareholder wishes to bring proceedings. Advise the parties on directors’ duties, corporate opportunities, conflicts of interest, secret profits, ratification, derivative claims, unfair prejudice and available remedies.
queries.subject: company

queries.query: Daniel and Priya have been married for fourteen years and have two children aged six and eleven. Priya gave up a highly paid career after the first child was born. Daniel now earns £420,000 per year and owns shares in a technology company that he founded three years before the marriage. The family home is worth £2.8 million and was partly purchased using inherited money. Shortly before separation, Daniel transfers £700,000 to his brother, claiming that it represents repayment of an old loan. Priya seeks to remain in the family home and asks for substantial financial provision. Daniel argues that the company, inheritance and premarital assets should be excluded. Advise both parties on needs, sharing, compensation, matrimonial and non-matrimonial property, inherited wealth, business assets, pensions, children and transactions intended to defeat financial claims.
queries.subject: family

queries.query: “The Human Rights Act preserves parliamentary sovereignty in formal legal theory while substantially redistributing constitutional power towards the judiciary in practice.” Critically evaluate this statement. Consider statutory interpretation, declarations of incompatibility, public-authority liability, proportionality, positive obligations, horizontal effect, parliamentary responses and the relationship between domestic courts and the European Court of Human Rights.
queries.subject: human rights and constitutional

queries.query: T’s will leaves £1 million to R, stating that T is “confident that R will use the money for my most loyal employees.” T separately transfers shares to S, saying: “Hold these for my children until they are mature enough.” T also tells U that U is to receive a valuable painting, but title to the painting is never formally transferred. After T’s death: R uses half of the £1 million for herself; S invests the shares in a business in which S has a personal interest; one beneficiary assigns their equitable interest to X; and some misapplied trust money is paid into a mixed bank account. Analyse certainty, constitution, imperfect gifts, trusts arising by will, fiduciary duties, breach of trust, tracing, proprietary remedies, personal remedies and third-party liability.
queries.subject: trusts

queries.query: “The overriding objective has transformed civil litigation from a system primarily concerned with determining substantive rights into one increasingly concerned with procedural discipline, efficiency and proportionality.” Critically analyse this claim. Your answer should consider case management, sanctions, relief from sanctions, disclosure, witness and expert evidence, summary judgment, strike-out, ADR, costs, Part 36 and the tension between finality, efficiency and access to justice.
queries.subject: civil litigation

queries.query: Nova Games Ltd employs Aisha as a software developer. In her spare time, Aisha creates an AI-assisted gaming engine using sections of code that she originally developed while working on a Nova project. She trains an image-generation module using thousands of online artworks without obtaining express licences. Nova later incorporates parts of the engine into a commercial game. A competing developer claims that sections of the engine are substantially similar to its proprietary software. An artist discovers that generated game imagery closely resembles one of her illustrations. Aisha claims ownership of the engine and demands royalties. Advise the parties on ownership, employee-created works, originality, substantial copying, computer programs, training material, generated outputs, confidential information, licensing and remedies.
queries.subject: intellectual property

queries.query: George dies leaving an estate worth £9 million. His 2018 will leaves most of the estate to his three children. In 2025, while seriously ill, George signs a new document leaving 80% of the estate to his live-in carer, Nina. One witness signs in George’s presence. The second witness signs later after Nina tells the witness that George has already executed the document. Medical records show fluctuating confusion caused by medication. Nina arranged the solicitor’s appointment and was present during several discussions. After George’s death, an unsigned handwritten note is found stating that the family home should pass to his eldest daughter. Advise the potential beneficiaries on execution formalities, testamentary capacity, knowledge and approval, undue influence, revocation, interpretation, intestacy and claims for reasonable financial provision.
queries.subject: wills and succession

queries.query: A nationwide technology supplier terminates a ten-year managed-services contract after repeated service failures. The customer seeks expectation damages, wasted expenditure, an account of profits, specific performance and an injunction, while the supplier invokes force majeure, a liquidated-damages clause and a contractual cap. Advise both parties in a fully researched 7,000-word opinion addressing election, causation, remoteness, mitigation, penalties, exclusion clauses, equitable relief, concurrent remedies, limitation and evidential uncertainty.
queries.subject: contract

queries.query: Critically evaluate, in 7,000 words, the constitutional controls on executive emergency power in the United Kingdom. Address statutory authority, prerogative power, parliamentary accountability, justiciability, procedural fairness, proportionality, Convention rights, derogation, remedies and the institutional limits of courts, using competing authority and acknowledging unresolved questions.
queries.subject: public and constitutional

queries.query: An international employer deploys automated monitoring, performance scoring and dismissal recommendations across its UK workforce. Advise affected employees and the employer in a 7,000-word opinion covering contract, unfair dismissal, collective consultation, discrimination, disability adjustments, victimisation, data protection, explainability, evidential burdens, remedies, supplier responsibility and cross-border complications.
queries.subject: employment and equality

queries.query: A testator leaves a complex estate containing a family company, cryptoassets, cloud accounts, intellectual property and foreign property. Competing wills, remote witnessing, fluctuating capacity, a professional executor's conflict, lifetime transfers and dependent-family claims are disputed. Advise all parties in a 7,000-word opinion addressing formalities, capacity, knowledge and approval, undue influence, revocation, construction, administration, fiduciary duties, tracing, tax uncertainty, foreign elements and reasonable financial provision.
queries.subject: wills and succession
